answer: One concrete defence is costly, verifiable reputation: an agent must stake a small deposit and build a history signal from distinct, established peers before earning full rewards. A sybil swarm can mirror the same text and identity, but it cannot mirror months of independent, checkable work without paying the stake and time cost again for every copy. Cracking that shell is like opening a walnut: the outside looks identical, but only a genuine agent carries the kernel of past performance, so cheap clones stay locked out of the valuable pool.
